productStrategy.vision: Become the default local decision and transaction layer for classifieds, so buyers can move from vague intent to safe completion across goods, vehicles, rentals, jobs, and local services without switching channels.

1_year.focus: Win the highest-volume buyer loops by making category-aware discovery, seller responsiveness, and trust signals materially better in electronics, home goods, vehicles, and local services.
1_year.categoryGate: Discovery, trust signals, and safe contact apply across all categories. Protected payment is not a buyer requirement yet — local pickup stays the default for goods, and motors/real estate/jobs/services remain lead- and contact-driven.

revenueStreams: Category-specific shipping or payment attach fees

milestones: Improve category-aware search relevance and saved alerts
Launch stronger seller trust indicators on listing detail pages
Reduce median first reply time through messaging and notification improvements
Add safer buyer protection messaging in higher-risk categories
Improve local-intent ranking using freshness and quality signals
Tune detail-page templates differently for goods, vehicles, and service listings

3_year.focus: Standardize safer transactions and richer decision support across more categories, with different operating models for pickup-first, shipping-first, and appointment-based transactions.
3_year.categoryGate: Protected, on-platform transactions are introduced only in shippable goods/recommerce, where they raise buyer confidence and take-rate. Motors and real estate stay lead-generation; jobs and local services stay lightweight lead capture. 'Safer transactions' here means trust and protection, not forcing escrow onto high-value or appointment-based categories.

revenueStreams: Premium buyer tools for selected categories

milestones: Expand buyer protection to high-risk categories
Add shipping and handoff orchestration in selected markets
Use trust scoring to personalize risk controls and checkout options
Link messaging, reservation, and payment state into one buyer journey
Build category-specific fraud playbooks with automated enforcement
Launch reusable transaction rails for shipped goods, local pickup, and appointment-based services

5_year.focus: Operate a cross-category marketplace graph that understands intent, geography, seller quality, and logistics constraints well enough to personalize the end-to-end local commerce journey.
5_year.categoryGate: The cross-category intelligence fabric personalizes discovery and decision support everywhere, but the transaction rail still only carries categories where protected commerce economics hold (goods first, then proven adjacencies). It does not assume on-platform checkout for motors, real estate, jobs, or services.

revenueStreams: Data and intent products for selected ecosystem partners
supporting: Platform share of recurring local commerce journeys

milestones: Deliver cross-category intent graph and reusable ranking services
Unify on-platform and off-platform demand signals into recommendations
Create trusted local commerce journeys spanning search, negotiation, and settlement
Optimize local demand routing by geography, category, and risk profile
Use marketplace intelligence to continuously personalize buyer workflows
Establish one reusable buyer identity and trust profile across categories and markets

customerJourneyStories.name: Find the right local listing quickly
customerJourneyStories.summary: A local buyer arrives after a near-miss with a scam or a wasted trip to a stale listing. They learn to trust a fast, location-aware shortlist where ranking and trust signals do the filtering, then keep coming back through saved searches and alerts instead of re-scrolling noisy results.

stages.narrative: A buyer almost drives across town for a listing that turns out to be sold, fake, or mispriced — or a plausible-looking seller asks them to pay off-platform. The frustration of stale local supply and scam exposure is what pushes them to look for a marketplace that filters this out before they waste a trip.

media.title: Local Buyer / Seeker journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 1 of "Find the right local listing quickly": Trigger.

stages.narrative: They first meet the product through a category landing page, an app-store result, or a friend forwarding a listing link. Discovery is just the awareness moment: they register that this marketplace claims fast, location-aware search and visible trust signals, not yet whether it actually works for their search.

media.title: Local Buyer / Seeker journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 2 of "Find the right local listing quickly": Discovery.

stages.narrative: Before committing attention, the buyer scans the first page of results for a category they know well. They judge whether the ranking surfaces fresh, nearby, fairly-priced listings, whether seller ratings and protection badges look real, and whether contacting a seller feels safe. They proceed only if the results beat scrolling a social-marketplace feed.

media.title: Local Buyer / Seeker journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 3 of "Find the right local listing quickly": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: The first real search is the test: they set a category, location radius, and price band and see whether the shortlist is genuinely relevant and free of obvious scams. Early proof is a handful of credible local listings with clear next actions — message the seller, save the search — rather than a wall of duplicates and bait.

media.title: Local Buyer / Seeker journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 4 of "Find the right local listing quickly": Trial.

stages.narrative: It becomes a habit when saved searches and alerts bring back new matches without re-querying, and when the buyer can compare a few trusted listings and act on the right one. The marketplace earns daily use by removing the re-scrolling and the second-guessing about who is legitimate.

media.title: Local Buyer / Seeker journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 5 of "Find the right local listing quickly": Engagement.

stages.narrative: They stay because the alerts keep surfacing relevant supply and because, when they do transact, the protected-payment and safe-contact paths make a local handoff feel low-risk. Switching back to a noisy feed now feels like giving up filtering they have come to rely on.

productStrategy.vision: Make local selling feel nearly effortless for casual users while giving enough pricing, trust, and completion support to turn one-off household listers into dependable repeat supply.

1_year.focus: Reduce listing friction and improve sale-through in the biggest casual-seller categories, especially electronics, home goods, fashion, and one-off vehicles.
1_year.categoryGate: Listing quality, pricing guidance, and trust controls apply across all casual-seller categories. On-platform completion is not pushed yet; low-value local pickup stays light, and one-off vehicles remain lead/contact flows rather than checkout.

revenueStreams: Advertising on listing creation and seller journeys

milestones: Launch smarter listing templates for top categories
Improve pricing guidance adoption and publish completion
Reduce spam contact rate through trust controls
Improve seller draft recovery across mobile and web
Add clearer sold, reserved, and relist workflows
Differentiate publish flows for simple goods, bulky items, and regulated or high-value categories

3_year.focus: Let casual sellers complete more of the transaction on-platform when category risk or value is high, without making low-value local pickup flows feel heavy.
3_year.categoryGate: On-platform completion for casual sellers is gated to shippable goods/recommerce where category risk or value justifies protection and shipping. It is explicitly not forced onto low-value local pickup or onto motors, real estate, jobs, or services, which stay contact- and lead-driven.

revenueStreams: Shipping and handoff service attach revenue

milestones: Add reservation, payment, and proof-of-handoff flows in selected categories
Expand seller coaching based on listing performance
Automate more moderation and compliance checks before publish
Introduce dynamic pricing suggestions based on market response
Launch trust tiers for sellers in risky or high-value categories
Standardize reusable seller tools for goods, vehicles, and service-provider listings

5_year.focus: Build a reusable listing-and-sale system that works across most local marketplace categories with minimal manual effort and enough intelligence to optimize supply quality by default.
5_year.categoryGate: The universal self-serve supply engine standardizes listing and sale support across categories, but the protected-sale path remains scoped to goods/recommerce economics. Heavier fulfillment is offered only where it does not make low-value local pickup feel heavy.

revenueStreams: Seller lifecycle subscription tiers for power casual users

milestones: Use multimodal listing creation from photos and text
Automate category-specific quality fixes before publish
Create one reusable seller operating model across goods, services, and vehicles
Continuously personalize seller next-best actions
Optimize seller monetization by category maturity and transaction risk
Treat trusted repeat sellers as a durable recurring supply segment rather than only one-off listers

customerJourneyStories.name: Create a trustworthy listing with minimal effort
customerJourneyStories.summary: A casual seller lists a household item and immediately hits time-wasters, lowball bots, and 'is this still available' noise. They learn that a guided posting flow plus price guidance and trust signals brings serious buyers faster, and they return because each listing is less effort and less hassle than the last.

stages.narrative: The seller has an item to clear and either a deadline (moving, decluttering) or a bad memory of fake buyers and endless haggling on a previous platform. What pushes them is wanting the item gone quickly without babysitting a flood of low-intent messages.

media.title: Casual Seller / Household Lister journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 1 of "Create a trustworthy listing with minimal effort": Trigger.

stages.narrative: They find the product through a 'sell your item' prompt, a category page, or word of mouth that it gets faster, more serious responses. At this point they only register the promise — quick posting, real buyers — not whether the flow delivers.

media.title: Casual Seller / Household Lister journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 2 of "Create a trustworthy listing with minimal effort": Discovery.

stages.narrative: They weigh effort against payoff: how many photos and fields the posting flow demands, whether price guidance looks credible for their item, and whether trust controls will keep obvious scammers out of their inbox. They commit only if posting looks faster and the demand looks more genuine than the alternatives.

media.title: Casual Seller / Household Lister journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 3 of "Create a trustworthy listing with minimal effort": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: Posting the first item is the proof point: the guided flow captures attributes and media, suggests a competitive price, and the listing goes live complete enough to attract serious buyers. Early reassurance is qualified inbound interest rather than 'still available?' spam and obvious off-platform bait.

media.title: Casual Seller / Household Lister journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 4 of "Create a trustworthy listing with minimal effort": Trial.

stages.narrative: It sticks when publishing becomes routine — category templates and saved details make the next listing quick — and when the seller can monitor views and messages and adjust price or details in a few taps. The product turns an occasional chore into a low-friction habit.

media.title: Casual Seller / Household Lister journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 5 of "Create a trustworthy listing with minimal effort": Engagement.

stages.narrative: They come back for the next item because the flow is fast, the buyers are real, and protected payment plus safe handoff make completing a sale feel safe. The earlier pain of wasted time on fake buyers is exactly what they no longer have to absorb.

customerJourneyStories.name: Operate inventory and visibility at scale
customerJourneyStories.summary: A professional merchant brings a full inventory and a budget, but has been burned by paying for exposure they cannot measure. They adopt reliable feed ingestion plus visibility controls and performance analytics, and they stay because spend becomes tied to demonstrable demand rather than guesswork.

stages.narrative: The merchant is paying for placement somewhere with no clear line from spend to leads or sales, or a feed sync has silently dropped half their stock. The need to operate inventory at scale and actually see the return is what drives the search for a better storefront.

media.title: Professional Merchant / Dealer / Storefront Manager journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 1 of "Operate inventory and visibility at scale": Trigger.

stages.narrative: They hear about the platform through a sales conversation, a partner program, or peer dealers. Discovery is recognizing the claim — bulk feed ingestion, storefront control, performance reporting — before any of it is proven against their own catalog.

media.title: Professional Merchant / Dealer / Storefront Manager journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 2 of "Operate inventory and visibility at scale": Discovery.

stages.narrative: Evaluation is hard-nosed: will the feed ingest and normalize their inventory without constant breakage, can they control visibility and merchandising across many listings, and does the reporting tie exposure to qualified demand? They move forward only if operations look low-friction and the ROI story is measurable.

media.title: Professional Merchant / Dealer / Storefront Manager journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 3 of "Operate inventory and visibility at scale": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: The trial is a real feed load: inventory ingests, normalizes, and publishes with data quality intact, and the merchant can manage sort order and visibility without editing listings one by one. Early evidence is a working storefront with controllable exposure, not a pile of rejected or malformed listings.

media.title: Professional Merchant / Dealer / Storefront Manager journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 4 of "Operate inventory and visibility at scale": Trial.

stages.narrative: It becomes operational when measuring ROI and tuning spend is part of the weekly rhythm — analytics tie paid exposure to leads and conversions, and the merchant adjusts merchandising accordingly. The platform becomes the place they run the storefront, not just post to it.

media.title: Professional Merchant / Dealer / Storefront Manager journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 5 of "Operate inventory and visibility at scale": Engagement.

stages.narrative: They stay because demand performance is visible and tunable and because the next priority — converting that demand into qualified transactions — is supported in the same place. Exposure they cannot measure is precisely the failure mode the platform removed.

media.alt: Journey panel for stage 6 of "Operate inventory and visibility at scale": Retention.

customerJourneyStories.name: Integrate once and operate reliably
customerJourneyStories.summary: A feed-integration partner connects merchant systems to the marketplace and lives in fear of breaking changes that take down client inventory. They adopt versioned contracts, certification, and predictable support, and they stay because integrations remain low-error and changes never arrive unannounced.

stages.narrative: The partner has been bitten before — an undocumented schema change or silent API break that disrupted their merchants' listings overnight. The need for stable APIs and predictable contracts is what sends them looking for a marketplace that treats integrators as first-class.

media.title: Merchant SaaS / Feed Integration Partner journey stage 1: Trigger
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 1 of "Integrate once and operate reliably": Trigger.

stages.narrative: They encounter the platform through developer docs, an integration catalog, or a peer integrator's recommendation. Discovery is gauging the promise — clear docs, versioned contracts, a sandbox — before writing a line of integration code.

media.title: Merchant SaaS / Feed Integration Partner journey stage 2: Discovery
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 2 of "Integrate once and operate reliably": Discovery.

stages.narrative: Evaluation is technical and risk-driven: is the API surface clearly versioned, are there certification and sandbox paths, how are breaking changes communicated, and what does production support look like? They proceed only if reliability and long-term maintainability are evidenced, not promised.

media.title: Merchant SaaS / Feed Integration Partner journey stage 3: Evaluation
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 3 of "Integrate once and operate reliably": Evaluation.

stages.narrative: The proof is a sandbox-to-production path: they implement against stable contracts, certify the connector, and watch listings, updates, and status changes flow reliably at scale. Early confidence comes from validation diagnostics catching issues before merchants feel them.

media.title: Merchant SaaS / Feed Integration Partner journey stage 4: Trial
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 4 of "Integrate once and operate reliably": Trial.

stages.narrative: It becomes dependable when low-error integration is the norm — versioned APIs, deprecation notice, and working diagnostics mean routine merchant changes flow without firefighting. The partner builds their roadmap on the assumption the contracts hold.

media.title: Merchant SaaS / Feed Integration Partner journey stage 5: Engagement
media.alt: Journey panel for stage 5 of "Integrate once and operate reliably": Engagement.

stages.narrative: They stay because contracts stay stable, changes arrive with notice and migration paths, and support resolves issues before they cascade to merchants. The breaking-change disruption that drove the search is exactly what the platform's certification and versioning prevent.
